lens: LUCK AND MULTIPLE COMPARISONS (permutation tests, game-clustered CI, leave-one-game-out, drop top games, Bonferroni for tried_count=522)
rule: R8 Late sniper: at 5 min before the start buy every listed bet with EV >= 2.5% (last c/w price look, listed, <=7 min old)
numbers_reproduced: Reproduced exactly with my own implementation of the selection: 28 bets, 16 games, 22 with a close (15 games), 12.41 bets/day over 2.256 days. CLV at the T-5 look 3.7186% game-clustered 95% CI [2.82%, 4.60%] (builder [2.81%, 4.59%]); 91% beat the close; same 22 bets at first look 2.865% (builder baseline 2.95%, paired gain +0.85 pts vs builder +0.77: small difference in how the baseline is taken, no effect on the verdict). Builder's halves reproduce only with a split Oct 3 | Oct 4-5 by start day (6 closes/5 games +4.01% | 16 closes/10 games +3.61%); the shared loader's split_by_date cuts at Oct 4 and leaves 20 closes before and 2 after. ROI at the T price -17.4% on 26 settled (16 games), game CI [-58.8%, +23.3%]. Paired sign-flip p for the gain over first look = 0.0060 (bet-level) and 0.0061 (game-level), matches the builder's 0.006. Close mix of the 22: 16 Tracker (all Tj-placed bets, 12 of them 'CNO's books'), 5 Novig last trades (9-48 trades), 1 Pinnacle.
reason: Not credible as an improvement; the apparent significance is a circularity/selection artifact and the multiple-comparison bill is unpaid. (1) The headline CLV is Tracker-driven: Tracker closes (16 of 22, CLV +4.90% [4.27, 5.44] on 12 games) are CNO-consensus reads made at about the same time as the look, so CLV tracks the listed EV (EV at the look 3.73%, CLV 4.90%, correlation 0.75 between EV at the look and CLV across the 41 Tracker-closed bets listed at T-5 (0.04 for the 43 Novig-trades closes)). The independent closes (5 Novig trades + 1 Pinnacle) give +0.58% on 6 bets/5 games, t-interval [-0.30%, +1.45%] (the game bootstrap [0.15%, 1.3%] on 5 games is not trustworthy); drop the single Pinnacle bet and it is +0.27% (5 Novig-trades bets, mean 0.27%, i.e. zero). Listed EV on those 6 was 3.38%, so ~90% of the EV vanished. (2) The 'paired gain' over the first look (+0.85 pts, p 0.006) is explained by selecting on EV at the T look: listed EV rose by +0.70 pts (2.93% to 3.63%) and CLV by +0.85 pts; net of EV the late-timing gain is +0.15 pts (t 0.82, p 0.42 t-test, 0.18 game-level sign-flip). (3) Placebo times: the same rule at T=1,2,3,7,10,15 min gives CLV +3.4% to +4.3% and at T=60 +6.4% (5 closes), independent closes +0.5% to +1.2% at every T: lateness is not what produces the number. (4) Permutation tests (20000 draws each, observed 3.719%): same-size random draws from the 97 closed bets listed at T-5: p<5e-5 uniform, 0 of 20000 game-level; stratified by close source p<5e-5; label shuffle within start day x close source p 0.00025 (Bonferroni x522 = 0.13); whole-study first-look uniform draws p 0.0043 (Bonferroni 1.0). The EV-matched null (whole-study bets with EV>=2.5% and a close, same close-source mix, at their first look; mean 2.16%) gives p 0.128. Independent closes only: p 0.177 vs random 6-draws from the 50 independent closes at T-5 (pool mean -0.11%). The small p-values in the first rows measure 'high listed EV predicts a CNO-based close', not a timing edge. (5) Multiple comparisons: the gain over first look has p 0.006; with tried_count 522 Bonferroni gives 3.1 (cap 1.0), family-wise P(at least one variant this good by chance) = 1-(1-0.006)^522 = 0.96 (0.26 if only ~50 variants are effectively independent, 0.11 for 20); the expected best null t over 522 independent tests is 3.4 vs the observed 2.70. To survive Bonferroni at 522 a p below 9.6e-5 is needed. (6) Not driven by one or two games: leave-one-game-out CLV 3.48% to 3.99%; drop the top 1/2/3/5 games 3.51/3.21/2.99/2.65%, all CIs above zero. That robustness is a property of the Tracker closes, so it does not rescue the claim. (7) Volume: 12.4 bets/day (28 bets, thin); only 6 of 28 (2.7 a day) have an independent close.
caveats: Sample is about 2.26 days; the 22 closes sit in 15 games, 5 of which carry the 6 independent closes. Any statement about a late-sniping edge is untestable on this log.
Closes exist only where Tj also placed the bet (Tracker) or the game had a Novig trades/Pinnacle/ESPN close; the 6 of 28 bets with no close are unaccounted for (selection on having a close).

A Novig-trades close read minutes after a T-5 buy is mostly Novig's own price a few minutes later, so ~0 CLV from it is close to mechanical for a late buy and says little about value either way; only the single Pinnacle close (+2.14%) is a sharp close.
ROI -17.4% on 26 settled is noise (CI [-58.8%, +23.3%]); it neither supports nor refutes the rule.
I could not rebuild the 522 variants, so the multiple-comparison numbers use K=522 (Bonferroni, independent-tests formula) and sensible effective K of 20 to 50 as brackets, not the exact family.

What would settle it: a late-vs-early comparison on INDEPENDENT closes (Pinnacle/Novig trades >=3) needs about 29 independent closes to see a +1 pt effect (SD 1.9 pts, 80% power) or 7 to see +2 pts; at 2.7 independent-close bets a day that is ~11 days for 29 (about 18 days for 49 to be safe), counting games not bets (roughly 25-40 games). To detect it Tj's study would also need to log a Pinnacle close for props (393 started bets have none).

Any change to which bets are bought at what time is a QUESTION FOR TJ, not an action; nothing here argues for loosening a safety limit (pregame only, price tolerance, trap guard, sharp check). This analysis supports not adopting R8 on the present evidence.
